abstract: Natural conversations make both speech recognition and speaker attribution challenging for ASR, as speakers take turns, overlap, and reappear over time. We propose STAM-ASR, Speaker-Temporal Anchoring with Memory, a lightweight framework that extends an already pretrained AudioLLM for multi-speaker ASR. Without relying on an external diarization system, STAM-ASR learns speaker activity and speaker-aware representations directly from intermediate AudioLLM features. Hence providing explicit who and when cues to modulate the AudioLLM's semantic representation without explicit speech separation. STAM-ASR further maintains fixed-size speaker and conversational memories to carry complementary context across turns. We evaluate STAM-ASR on AMI, ICSI, LibriCSS, and NOTSOFAR-1 across close-talk, far-field, overlapping, and cross-domain conditions. Our reported results shows that speaker-temporal conditioning and memory provide complementary benefits, while the gap between reference and predicted speaker activity identifies robust speaker tracking as a key remaining challenge.

oneSentenceThesis: 针对多人轮替与重叠会议转写，STAM-ASR 在冻结 Qwen2.5-Omni-7B 编码器上加内部说话人日志、残差 FiLM 调制与说话人/会话双记忆，在参考与预测说话人活动对比中显示时间证据与记忆互补，但预测跟踪误差仍是主要瓶颈。
